text:
Priya (PM): FYI — big customer asks landed this morning: strict regional egress controls + latency-aware spillover. They want guarantees that PII never leaves EU unless explicitly allowed, but also expect <200ms p99. Need to scope roadmap and launch criteria. Thoughts?

Jordan (EngLead): I think model is layered policy: hard blocks for sensitive data, soft spillover for capacity with explicit consent + audit trail. We should avoid 'one-size-fits-all'.

Alex (Infra): We can tag traffic at the gateway and enforce at the dataplane. Need a control-plane API for per-tenant egress policies and an allowlist for spillover regions. Implementation risk is low; state is the tricky bit.

Liang (Runtime): Caveat: runtime caches (KV/prefix cache) aren't trivial to replicate across regions. Two approaches: replicate model state (costly) or route to a local fallback model (cheaper but lower quality). Both affect latency.

Rebecca (Security): Legal note — some customers require demonstrable zero cross-border requests (not just 'best effort'). That requires contract language + per-request audit logs. For Private installs we also need HSM/KMS locality assurances.

Brenda (PM): Proposed launch criteria (draft):
- enforcement mode (deny/allow/spill) available in canary region
- telemetry shows involuntary cross-region <0.5% after canary
- documented failover behavior and billing implications
- customer-facing docs + contract clause templates

Sara (SRE): Ops requirements: circuit breakers for region saturation, emergency blackhole for a tenant, drain playbook for forced regional evacuation. Alerts when cross-region errors or latency spikes > threshold.

Mateo (Sales): Confirming demand: two large fintechs asked for hard egress + audit logs. They'll sign Dedicated + Private for the feature. Suggest pricing as an add-on: 'Regional Egress Compliance'.

Tom (Account Exec): Add this flag to new contracts: "Data Processing Region(s)" + "Allowed Spillover Regions" checkbox. Also define penalty/SLA if we spill without consent.

Priya (PM): Decision proposal: build a policy DSL with three primitives: deny, allow-list, spillover (with SLO guardrails). Expose via Console + API. Scope for MVP: control-plane + enforce at edge for routing; runtime fallback as opt-in.

Jordan (EngLead): I'll prototype enforcement and a minimal UI for policy editing. Also will sketch telemetry counters: cross_region_count, spillover_approved_count, spillover_latency_ms_histogram.

Jordan (EngLead): example policy config I'll prototype:
```yaml
tenant_policy:
  home_region: eu-west-1
  egress:
    mode: deny
    allowed_spillovers:
      - eu-central-1
    spillover_slo_ms: 200
    spillover_max_rate_per_min: 5
```

Liang (Runtime): For the prototype I'll benchmark two options: local quantized fallback (gives ~2–5% QA drop, 30–50ms faster) vs warm replica (no QA drop, +cost & +replication latency). Put numbers in the doc.

Rebecca (Security): Add requirement: per-request immutable audit record (region, route, model, decision reason). Must be exportable for compliance reviews.

Sara (SRE): Ops note: add an automated rollback trigger if spillover error-rate > 2% or p99 latency > 2x baseline for 5m. Also need a canary path for Tenant A/B testing of spillover.

Priya (PM): Launch checklist items (working draft):
- Policy DSL v1 + API + Console (Jordan)
- Enforce at edge + dataplane tagging (Alex)
- Runtime fallback benchmark + recommendation (Liang)
- Audit logging per-request (Rebecca)
- Ops runbooks + alerting (Sara)
- Contract templates + pricing (Tom & Mateo)
- Customer communications + demo (Brenda)

Mateo (Sales): Please add a short FAQ for sales: what counts as "spillover", how billing works, what guarantees we provide.

Jordan (EngLead): Noted. I will add metrics/events to the telemetry schema:
- event:egress_decision {tenant, home_region, chosen_region, reason}
- metric:egress_spillover_count
- metric:egress_block_count

Alex (Infra): Implementation tip: use route-mapping at L7 with tenant metadata. If enforcement is required at L3/L4 for Private, we need an iptables-ish shim or service mesh rule generator. Extra engineering but doable.

Rebecca (Security): Also flag: remote logging of request payload is forbidden for 'deny' tenants. Ensure observability doesn't leak raw inputs to cross-region logging systems.

Brenda (PM): Can we get a rough timeline? Jordan, Liang, Alex — three-week spike to prototype + benchmarks? Then 4–6 weeks for MVP?

Jordan (EngLead): 3-week spike sounds reasonable. Will post milestone PRs to the thread.

Liang (Runtime): I'll prioritize the fallback benchmarks this week.

Sara (SRE): I'll prepare the runbook template and add the ciruit-breaker config to ops-templates repo.

Priya (PM): Great. Sync tomorrow 10am to review spike plan. @ops-bot please create meeting and add notes channel. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Meeting created — Thu 10:00 in #architecture. Invite sent to attendees.

Tom (Account Exec): :thinking_face: Also let's surface this in the legal intake flow so deals with residency needs route to Sec + Contracts immediately.

Priya (PM): Agreed. I'll add a checkbox in the intake form. Thanks all — we'll iterate after the spike updates.
